az_sharpie_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of a couple of granite boulders in the north Phoenix bouldering zone, tucked in among the larger slab boulders of the e-Boulders. Thirteen problems, all bouldering, and the bulk sit at the easy end: roughly eight at V0, one at VB, then a handful of V2 to V4 lines and a single much harder V6 problem. Problems are mostly short, so this is a quick stop for warm-ups and moderate circuits rather than a destination for a full day. It makes a convenient add-on if you are already climbing the nearby slabs. Bring a pad and look over the landings before you pull on.
az_sharpie_boulders.approach: From the Egg parking lot, head north and then follow the trail northwest past a few of the other e-Boulders to reach the cluster.

az_roost_area_the.blurb: The Roost is a cliff on the north side of Raptor Ridge in Queen Creek Canyon, near Superior in central Arizona. Of its 13 climbs, ten are trad and three are sport, spanning 5.9 up to 5.13, with most falling in the 5.9 to 5.10 range and only a few hard lines at the top end. The lines are long and sustained for the canyon, which suits climbers wanting endurance mileage over short pitches. The face stays shady, so it works best in warmer months; the west side picks up sun late in the day and has shorter routes. A rack and a head for committing climbing help here.

az_barracuda_boulders.blurb: A cluster of boulders in Euro Dog Valley, part of the Oak Flat bouldering in Queen Creek Canyon, sitting near the campground boulder in the valley. All thirteen problems are bouldering, and they are gentle: one VB, about five at V0, a few V1 and V2 problems, and a single V3 as the hardest. Most can be done safely with pads and a spotter, and a few are set up as top-rope problems, so it suits beginners and families getting started outdoors. Most of the boulders hold shade through the morning, making early starts pleasant when it warms up.

az_red_diamond_wall.blurb: A steep, secluded wall in the mid-mountain zone of Mount Lemmon, in the Santa Catalina Mountains north of Tucson, where the climbing sits in cool pine forest well above the desert heat. Thirteen climbs, mostly trad with a few sport lines, run from 5.9 into the low 5.12s, with the weight in 5.10 and 5.11. Routes are long single pitches with an adventurous feel on granite with plates and incuts. The wall faces east, so it gets the morning sun and goes into shade by afternoon. Expect a quiet day compared with the road-side crags.

az_time_zone.blurb: A sunny south-facing granite wall on the west shore of Watson Lake in the Granite Dells near Prescott. Thirteen climbs, mostly trad plus a couple of sport lines and a top-rope, and the grades are easy to moderate: from 5.2 up to 5.9, with most between 5.5 and 5.7. That makes it a popular pick for beginners, groups and anyone wanting a mellow day, and it can get busy. The setting of rounded granite domes and boulders beside the lake is often compared to Joshua Tree. The south aspect keeps it warm, so it is a good cool-season destination.

az_pottery_wall.blurb: A striped limestone wall in Priest Draw, a small canyon south of Flagstaff, standing almost straight across the wash from the main parking lot. This is a hard-end bouldering wall: all thirteen problems fall between V7 and V12, with the bulk in V8 and V9. A low roof at the base leads into steep, mostly overhanging face climbing on pockets, and several of the lines are long traverses along the pocket row, some with stand-start variations on the left. Not a place for warm-ups; plan to bring easier problems from the neighbouring walls to get ready.
az_pottery_wall.approach: Cross the wash from the main parking lot; the wall is almost directly opposite, a very short walk.

az_whining_dog_wall.blurb: A friendly bouldering wall on the Drysdale Trail at The Ridge, east of Flagstaff near Lake Mary, at about 7,000 feet. Thirteen problems, nearly all easy: one VB, about five at V0, a few V1, then a handful from V2 to V4. The face bulges nicely and offers good holds, so it works well for traverses and plenty of variations, and it is widely regarded as one of the best moderate walls in the Flagstaff area. A good choice for warming up, introducing newer boulderers, or linking easy mileage before heading to harder walls along the trail.

az_africa_boulder.blurb: A small bouldering spot in Pima Canyon on South Mountain, inside the city's mountain park in Phoenix, with the main boulder sitting in the wash just below the amphitheatre. Thirteen problems range from an easy V0 up to V11, but the middle is where most of the fun is, with the bulk at V2 to V4 and a few strong V5 to V9 lines for people looking to push. Several are well-regarded classics. Bees are often found near the base, more so after rain.
az_africa_boulder.approach: Walk the Pima Canyon dirt road for roughly a mile, then continue up the wash; the boulder is just before the scramble up to the amphitheatre.

_conflicts.az_roost_area_the: Stored rock is basalt; the Queen Creek Canyon parent page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105788089/queen-creek-canyon) calls the canyon rock volcanic tuff. Not changed; blurb does not name the rock.
